title: Arkret Standard Event Payloads
description: Definitions bundle for common payload contracts used by registered ak.* Event.kind values. The root schema is intentionally generic and MUST NOT be used as a complete payload validator. Event validators MUST validate the full Event Envelope and dispatch by Event.kind to the matching $defs payload class using artifacts/registry/event-kind-registry.json.

not.$comment: The event-payload schema root is a definition-bundle diagnostic only. Standard payload validation MUST select one explicit kind-bound schema ref from the event kind registry.

account_blocklist_payload.description: Payload for ak.account.blocklist. Holder-private personal blocklist state; it never enters shared Realm state or federation payloads.

version.description: Monotonic whole-value CAS revision. The next accepted ak.account.blocklist payload MUST use current version + 1; ak.account_data.set for key ak.account.blocklist uses expected_revision against the same counter. Omitting an entry in the next revision removes it, and entries=[] clears the list.

mode.description: block denies a new holder-facing interaction on the selected surfaces and filters shared durable content only after canonical receive/store; mute keeps content visible but suppresses attention surfaces; hide keeps canonical content but omits it from default holder rendering/search. None of the modes revokes a Realm capability or rewrites shared history.

account_data_set_payload.description: Payload for ak.account_data.set. Writes one holder-private account-data key; the value may be plaintext inside an already private envelope, encrypted account-data material, or a tombstone. Every key is a compare-and-set whole-value register per zh/models/account-data.md §5: expected_revision is the revision the writer believes is current (0 to create), and the accepted revision is expected_revision + 1.

expected_revision.description: Compare-and-set precondition against the accepted per-key revision. A mismatch MUST be rejected with cas_conflict and MUST NOT be stored; the revision counter is a high-water mark that never goes backwards, so a stale offline retry cannot resurrect a superseded value.

body.description: Caller-supplied opaque account-data value. Any JSON value.

actor_profile_create_payload.description: Initial actor profile payload. The materialized resolution projection is reducer-managed from the PCR resolution cell and is forbidden on this authoring surface. id/updated_by/updated_at are likewise materialized fields, not create input.

actor_profile_update_payload.description: Actor Profile patch payload. resolution and every resolution.* descendant path are reducer-managed projections of the PCR resolution cell and are forbidden on this generic profile write surface.

agent_action_approve_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.action_approve. Controller approval binds the draft/action request, target, approved payload digest, expiry, and single-use nonce.

agent_action_reject_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.action_reject. Controller rejection terminates a draft/action request without shared Realm side effects.

agent_action_request_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.action_request. Actor-private request for controller approval before a shared Realm write is emitted.

agent_action_target.description: Minimal target descriptor for an actor-private agent draft or approval. It identifies the eventual shared write surface without disclosing private draft content.

agent_deactivate_payload.description: Payload for the single terminal ak.self.agent.deactivate Control Move. At the accepted Seal covering this Move, every verifier mechanically AND-gates all subordinate Agent runtime-key authorizations, sessions, pairing handles, capability grants, KeyPackages, presence and future submissions on lifecycle=active. Historical child Events remain auditable; explicit child revokes are not prerequisites and are reserved for targeted revocation while the Agent is non-terminal. The lifecycle state witness is sufficient transition evidence for every derived ineffective child.

previous_status.description: Controller lifecycle intent at deactivation time. Generic Agent status has only lifecycle, readiness and presence; pairing-poll runtime_state is operation-local and never appears here (key-management.md §3.6.1).

agent_draft_propose_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.draft.propose. Actor-private proposal that may materialize into controller-owned encrypted draft account data after policy checks.

agent_key_approval_evidence.description: Evidence that authorized this agent key. Durable grant/approval/proposal/policy evidence carries ref so it can be replayed at the event frontier; the short-lived pairing_request branch instead binds pairing_request_id, request_canonical_digest, and approved_by and MUST omit ref.

pairing_request_id.description: Optional profile-local, short-lived pairing artifact id. Required by the agent-key pairing acceptance flow and MUST equal the pairing_request_id in the accepted request; it is not a durable protocol object ref.

agent_key_authorize_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.key.authorize. Binds one concrete agent signing key to an accountable principal, explicit agent_key_scope, audience, validity window, approval evidence, and both the service-surface and content-capability ceilings that later agent_key_proof sessions must narrow from.

public_key_digest.description: SHA-256 of the decoded 32-byte Ed25519 public key behind verification_method, computed with agent_signing_public_key_digest. Native Agent authorization always commits this raw-key digest; it is distinct from the private runtime-request PublicKey DTO digest.

signing_key_binding_digest.description: sha256 over the canonical agent-signing binding core containing schema, agent_id, agent_key_id, verification_method, public_key, public_key_digest, issued_at, optional expires_at, and controller_id, but excluding agent_key_authorize_event_id and controller_proof. The complete accepted Event ID and controller proof are appended only when materializing the public ak.schema.agent_signing_key_binding.v1 object. Including this Event's not-yet-derived identity would create an impossible digest fixed point. A service MUST recompute the core digest before appending the verified accepted Event identity and MUST NOT substitute another disclosure.

expires_at.description: Optional: absent means the key authorization is non-expiring and governed solely by revocation (ak.agent.key.revoke / lifecycle cascade).

supersedes.description: Exact set of every active Agent-key authorization dot observed immediately before this controller-signed authorization is accepted during runtime re-pairing. Each entry binds both the key id and the authorization Event that introduced the active dot. The array MUST be omitted only for first pairing, when the authoritative active set is empty. Every replacement MUST set-equal the complete pre-accept active authorization set, including an old dot with the same key_id as the new authorization; a stale, partial, extra, or implicit map overwrite fails closed. Acceptance atomically removes these dots with reason superseded_by_repairing and adds this authorize dot, so no server-forged ak.agent.key.revoke Event is required.

revocation_check_ref.description: Optional freshness source for revocation checking. When expires_at is absent, authorization lifetime is governed by the canonical revocation chain and lifecycle cascade; this field may identify the freshness source used for that check.

runtime_attestation.description: Optional runtime / workload attestation captured at pairing approval time. v1 enum includes self_asserted as baseline; future profiles MAY register TEE / SLSA / SPIFFE attestation kinds. Implementations encountering an unknown kind MUST fail closed.

kind.description: v1 enum. Future profiles MAY extend via accepted attestation taxonomy.

attestation_digest.description: Optional digest of verifiable attestation material when kind is not self_asserted.

attestation_ref.description: Optional external verifiable attestation reference (TEE quote, SLSA provenance, etc.).

agent_key_id.description: Stable key identifier within the agent DID. Prefer the DID URL verification method id when available.

agent_key_revoke_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.key.revoke. The or_set cell subject is (agent_id, key_id); future protocol proofs from this key fail closed once this event is covered by an accepted Seal. The authoring frontiers is the Control Move envelope seal_basis; the payload carries no frontier field.

agent_key_scope.description: Agent scope object with two uses. In POST /_arkret/self/agents requested_scope it is the required immutable global Agent ceiling; in ak.agent.key.authorize it is a per-key ceiling that MAY be narrower but MUST be an actions/resources/constraints subset of the provision ceiling. It is never a capability grant. actions may contain service operation ids and content action tokens; an omitted action can never be restored by a key, Realm grant or session. resources constrain the service surface and may optionally narrow later content resources, but never authorize content by themselves. Provisioning and pairing do not materialize capability grants from this object; effective authority is the intersection of provision ceiling, key ceiling, independent Realm-scoped grants, session request, membership and policy, with participation applied as an additional deny gate.

actions.description: Literal action ceiling. Every downstream key scope, grant or session action MUST appear here; action families, prefixes and subsumption do not widen it.

resources.description: Selector ceiling, not authorization. Each downstream selector must be covered by a parent selector. operation/service parents cover the same kind and matching explicit field and cannot carry content fields. The content-kind vocabulary is the ResourceSelector vocabulary except '*'; kind=realm covers every Realm-local content kind in the matching Realm and other content kinds cover only the same kind. Omitted parent realm_id is a cross-Realm ceiling wildcard and omitted exact ref is a same-kind/same-Realm wildcard. With no content selector, later Realm grants still choose concrete resources and no content wildcard is granted.

constraints.description: Global mandatory constraints. Every effective key/grant/session evaluation MUST retain and AND these constraints; downstream scopes may add stricter constraints but MUST NOT omit or relax provision constraints.

agent_pause_payload.description: Payload for ak.self.agent.pause. The status cell is keyed by agent_id and moves from active to paused. Authorization is evaluated against the Control Move envelope seal_basis; the reducer accepts the transition only under the accepted current control frontier.

agent_resume_payload.description: Payload for ak.self.agent.resume. Authorization is evaluated against the Control Move envelope seal_basis, and reducers re-check controller, agent, key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability grant against the accepted current control frontier before returning the agent to active. Sidecar desired membership is derived afterward and is not carried in this payload.

agent_sidecar_exchange_control_payload.description: Outer payload for ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control. sidecar_id and source_context_ref route the Event inside a native Sidecar scope; encrypted_payload plaintext MUST validate as agent-sidecar-exchange-control.schema.json. Admission MUST require matching scope_ref.kind=sidecar and actor_id equal to the Sidecar controller.

agent_slug.description: Controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug used by @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>. Not a global handle or authorization subject.

applet_bridge_error_payload.description: Payload for ak.applet.bridge_error. Durable Realm-history Event recording a bridge / external-network failure. Field table: zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §7. MUST bind realm_id, failed_transaction_ref, retriable, and visibility_scope; missing any required field MUST be rejected as schema_violation. MUST NOT inline unauthorized external plaintext.

failed_transaction_ref.description: Reference to the failed transaction / source Event. MUST NOT inline unauthorized external plaintext.

error_class.description: Closed error category for aggregation / alerting. See zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §7.

visibility_scope.description: Closed visibility scope enum for the error event. Clients MUST honor it and MUST NOT expose bridge-internal detail to unrelated members.

external_ref.description: External network reference (protocol / network id). MUST NOT contain unauthorized external plaintext.

message.description: Human-readable summary. MUST NOT leak unauthorized external plaintext.

retry_after_ms.description: Suggested retry delay; meaningful only when retriable=true.

applet_registration_payload.description: Payload for ak.applet.registration. Durable Realm-history Event registering an Applet (bridge / bot / Ghost Actor namespace). Field vocabulary: zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §4 and zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §1 (the authoritative machine schema is applet.schema.json, which documents the applet object snapshot; the wire Event payload is this closed class). An Applet's capability to enter a Realm MUST be granted by that Realm's owner / admin / authorized registry-authz service; a self-signed registration alone MUST NOT write to a Realm (reason=applet_registration_unauthorized). registration MUST be signed by the controller DID (proof per models/event-and-patch.md §3).

applet_id.description: Stable applet identifier: a DID or the typed-id form ak:applet:<uuidv7>.

service_id.description: DID of the service hosting the applet runtime.

controller_id.description: DID of the Applet controller / external system; signs the registration.

claimed_profiles.description: Canonical Applet implementation profiles copied from the accepted package. These durable claims are the authority source for profile-bound grant rules.

namespaces.description: Applet namespace claims (actors / realms / handles patterns). Namespace match alone never grants write capability.

webhook_auth.description: Transaction push HTTP signature policy copied from the Applet package. webhook_auth.key_ref is the Applet service DID URL used to verify the app/bridge->arkret inbound HTTP message signature and is bound to this registration_epoch; node->Applet pushes verify the Arkret source service DID from Source-Service-ID instead.

manifest.description: Applet manifest snapshot (capability requirements, supported intents, etc.).

proof.description: Controller-DID detached signature over the canonical registration object (excluding proof). An empty proof object MUST be rejected as schema_violation; required proof fields per models/event-and-patch.md §3.

audience_mention_node.description: Broadcast mention AST node carried in a Content Block `audience_mentions[]`. It is never expanded into `mention_node` entries in shared history; recipient expansion happens receiver-side under the ak.message.mention.broadcast, audience policy, max_recipients and quota gates in zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.3-§9.4.4.

audience.description: Canonical audience selector. @here maps to strand_engaged and is never presence-filtered; presence-filtered audiences require a separate declared profile.

audit_accessed_payload.description: Strict payload for ak.audit.accessed. It records a specific access or paired privacy-sensitive write. Reducers MUST reject business events that require an audit pair unless this payload identifies the same writer, target, and object/cell in the same ordered submit batch, equivalent control transaction, or an accepted pre-read event with RYW receipt.

late_recovery_original_event_id.description: Required when access_kind=e2ee_late_recovery; identifies the original encrypted event whose plaintext became available through late key recovery.

ryw_required.description: When true, plaintext release or privileged projection MUST wait for an accepted-history RYW receipt before disclosure.

audit_applet_binding_create_payload.description: Genesis payload for ak.audit.applet_binding.create. binding_id, initial active status, creator, and creation time are derived from the accepted Event envelope. Policy fields are immutable; changing them creates a new binding so historical release eligibility cannot be silently expanded.

activation_frontier_digest.description: Accepted Seal coverage digest at which this binding/policy became member-visible. Release requests MUST NOT cover messages or epochs before this coverage point.

first_auditable_epoch.description: First MLS epoch eligible for this binding. Reducers MUST verify it is the epoch created by a ak.mls.commit covering activation_frontier_digest; earlier epochs are permanently ineligible.

retroactive_release.description: v1 audited E2EE never permits a later binding or policy expansion to make pre-activation messages auditable.

eligibility_basis.description: A message is eligible only if it was encrypted after a commit covering this binding/policy frontier.

max_lookback_ms.description: Optional maximum age, measured from session request/authorization time, for otherwise eligible material. Later policy changes may narrow this for future messages but MUST NOT expand already encrypted messages.

max_epoch_span.description: Optional cap on the number of sealed historical epochs a single session/release may cover.

allowed_target_kinds.description: Optional target class allow-list for targeted_evidence_release.

audit_applet_binding_state_payload.description: Lifecycle-only transition for an existing Audit Applet Binding. Scope and release policy cannot be edited by this Event; a policy change requires a new binding genesis.

audit_release_payload.description: Payload for ak.audit.release. A sealed audit release manifest for a bounded historical window. It appends to the control-plane ordered log ak.component.audit.release.v1 keyed by session_id only while the accepted session FSM head is notice. Same-basis close dominates and rejects the release. The payload records release metadata and wrapped material digests only; plaintext MUST NOT be inlined.

recipient_public_key_ref.description: Release material encryption target. MUST equal the authorize payload's approved_recipient_public_key_ref and resolve to recipient_audit_actor_id's authorized audit-release key.

eligibility_proof.description: Proof summary that the requested release is inside the binding activation frontier, first_auditable_epoch, release_window_policy, and the targets' encryption-time eligibility snapshots.

activation_commit_ref.description: ak.mls.commit that covered the activation frontier and created first_auditable_epoch, when the release covers MLS epoch material.

policy_snapshot_digest.description: Digest of the binding/release window policy snapshot used when authorizing this release.

target_eligibility_digest.description: Digest of the deterministic per-target/per-epoch eligibility set proving no pre-activation material is included.

audit_session_contract.description: Shared payload class for ak.audit.session.request / authorize / notice / close. The session_state field is the target state of the control-plane FSM cell ak.component.audit.session.v1 keyed by session_id. Initial state is request; legal main-path transitions are request->authorize->notice->close, with request->close and authorize->close allowed for aborted sessions. Close is terminal; same-basis conflicting siblings produce Bottom.

approved_recipient_audit_actor_id.description: Audit subject approved to receive release material. Required on ak.audit.session.authorize; ak.audit.release.recipient_audit_actor_id MUST match it byte-for-byte.

approved_recipient_public_key_ref.description: Audit release recipient key approved by ak.audit.session.authorize. MUST resolve to approved_recipient_audit_actor_id's authorized audit-release key; ak.audit.release.recipient_public_key_ref MUST match it byte-for-byte.

board_space_id.description: A Space with kind=board. Pattern matches any ak:space:; kind invariant enforced by reducer/profile.

call_participant.description: A single participant value added by ak.call.state.payload.roster_delta. See crypto-media/call-state.md §4/§4.1.

foci_preferred.description: Client-local ordered focus preference list used for the session_focus election (see crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1 and media-service-binding.md §5).

participant_identity.description: Required for sfu/mcu roster joins; MUST be absent for a direct p2p/mesh leg.

participant_binding.description: Required for sfu/mcu roster joins; MUST be absent for a direct p2p/mesh leg. The containing call focus.mode selects the semantic branch.

call_recording_start_payload.description: Typed payload for ak.call.recording.start. recording_id is a stable opaque ASCII handle (1–128 bytes, [A-Za-z0-9._-]) that feeds the recording key exporter Context byte-for-byte and MUST NOT be normalized by receivers. capture_kind selects recording vs transcription so both lifecycles share one start event kind. See crypto-media/call-state.md §5 / §5.1.

recording_id.description: Stable opaque recording / transcript lifecycle handle. Canonical byte-for-byte; receivers MUST NOT normalize (case-fold, NFC/NFKC, trim, re-encode) because it is a cross-implementation key-derivation input.

capture_kind.description: Whether this start event opens a recording or a transcription segment. REQUIRED: it selects the target capture cell family (ak.component.call.recording.v1 vs ak.component.call.transcript.v1) in the registered cell contract, so it MUST NOT be inferred from a missing-field default.

visible_notice.description: Asserts the initiating client will display the capture-in-progress notice to all participants.

result.description: Initial immutable capture evidence. retention.consent_confirmed=true closes the pre-capture consent gate before the FSM enters a capturing state. This wire payload MUST NOT carry recording_start_event_id or transcript_start_event_id: the accepted Event identity is derived only after digesting this payload, and the reducer stamps that identity into the projected result cell.

call_create_payload.description: Genesis payload for ak.call.create. call_id is omitted and derived by retyping the accepted Event id. Signaling, media tokens, Morph bindings, and state deltas MUST reference only an already accepted create.

call_state_payload.description: Typed delta payload for ak.call.state. Every present field maps to one or two explicit registered cell effects; omitted axes produce no effect.

result.description: Typed recording outcome for a stopped, ready, or failed segment. It is written to the independent recording result cell and never embedded in the FSM transition op.

artifact.description: Canonical artifact metadata for recording_transition.to=ready. It binds the Arkret blob, recording exporter context, retention policy and deletion audit surface.

failure_message.description: Human-readable diagnostic for recording_state=failed. It MUST NOT contain recording plaintext or backend direct URLs.

result.description: Typed transcription outcome for a stopped, ready, or failed segment. It is written to the independent transcript result cell and never embedded in the FSM transition op.

call_summary_payload.description: Typed payload for ak.call.summary (durable end-of-call summary). Written once after a call reaches a terminal `state`; carries duration, peak participant count, and capture status so clients can render a durable call record without replaying ephemeral signaling. See crypto-media/call-state.md §7. started_at/ended_at/duration_ms are nullable: non-active terminal states (missed/cancelled/failed) MUST set them null per call-state.md §7.

final_state.description: The terminal call lifecycle state this summary closes over. MUST be one of the call_state_payload terminal states.

peak_participant_count.description: Highest concurrent participant count observed during the call.

distinct_participant_count.description: Number of distinct (actor_id, device_id) participants that joined at any point.

recording_state.description: Final recording_state at call end, mirrored from ak.call.state for the durable record. Absent = the call was not recorded.

transcript_state.description: Final transcript_state at call end, mirrored from ak.call.state. Absent = the call was not transcribed.

capability_grant_payload.description: Canonical ak.capability.grant genesis payload. Both top-level grant_id and grant.id are forbidden because the durable GrantId is derived by retyping this Event's event_id. issuer_principal_server_id, authority_depth and authority_root_refs are also forbidden in this closed authoring shape: after verifying grant.issuer equals the Event author, the reducer copies Event.principal_server_id into issuer_principal_server_id and derives the remaining audit members before writing the complete CapabilityGrant cell value. The Event envelope proof is the sole durable issuer signature.

capability_derived_payload.description: Reducer-authored cross-Realm capability derivation. Unlike capability genesis this references an existing Grant and therefore carries the already-derived grant_id and complete projected grant body, including the source grant's issuer_principal_server_id. A derived projection preserves that authority pair and MUST NOT replace it with a local reducer or receiving service identity.

capability_relinquish_payload.description: ak.capability.relinquish — subject-only release of the actor own grant. The authority is the target grant subject's signature, never a capability: a narrowly-scoped holder that was never granted ak.capability.revoke must still be able to give up what it holds. The reducer target guard accepts actor == target.subject and nothing else, so this can never become an unauthorized revocation. Descendants of the released grant fail through their issuer_authority_refs at read time.

circle_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the Circle object schema for wire validation. Reducer validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match top-level created_at, then enforce parent Realm encryption floor. When payload.object.encryption_profile='mls_rfc9420', the reducer derives the independent MLS group binding for (realm_id, circle_id). payload.object.mls_group_ref is reducer-derived and MUST NOT be actor supplied.

not.$comment: zh/models/common-fields.md: the object id is derived from this create Event's own event_id; carrying it in the payload is schema_violation reason object_id_not_event_derived.

circle_member_state_payload.description: Payload for ak.circle.member.state. Uses the same membership_state enum as ak.member.state (Realm), scoped to a Circle; reducer MUST verify actor_id is a `join` member of the parent Realm before any transition to `join`, MUST gate `knock` on Circle join_rule=knock, and MUST reject self-unban/self-unremove paths.

expected_membership.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency guard, orthogonal to the membership transition guard. The three wire states are distinct: omission applies no CAS and leaves legality to the FSM guard, explicit null asserts the actor currently has no membership record in this Circle, and a concrete value asserts the current membership equals it. A failed assertion MUST be rejected with failed_precondition. See zh/models/circle.md §9.1.

circle_patch_payload.description: Payload class for ak.circle.update. Patch path MUST NOT contain realm_id, encryption_profile, mls_group_ref, state, state_changed_at, created_by, or created_at; reducer enforces the path-level lock and semantic policy floor checks.

circle_seal_commit_payload.description: Reducer-derived payload for ak.circle.seal_commit. Commits an opaque Circle sub-seal head digest into the parent Realm Seal stream at the profile-defined cadence.

consent_grant_payload.description: Holder-private consent grant. The actor (consenter) is the holder; payload.peer is the counterparty whose contact is consented to. Wire-equivalent to a Move whose effect is add(tag,value) on the cell ak:cell:ak.component.consent.grant.v1:<consent_id> (or_set lattice); ak.consent.revoke writes a remove on the same cell. Lives in the holder's Principal Control Realm (or holder-private actor stream); MUST NOT be written to a shared Collaboration Realm. Realm role taxonomy: zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.7.

consent_id.description: Stable identifier; used as the cell_subject of the consent cell. ak.consent.revoke MUST reference the same consent_id.

peer.description: Counterparty DID (or pairwise DID) that this consent applies to.

consent_scope.description: What kind of contact is consented to. 'invite' = peer may send Realm / Strand invites; 'direct_message' = peer may initiate 1:1 message; 'voice_call' / 'video_call' = peer may initiate WebRTC call; 'presence' = peer may observe presence; 'any' = full consent across all consent scopes.

constraints.description: Optional consent-specific constraints (rate limits, time-of-day windows, device restrictions). v1 does not standardise constraint types beyond capability constraint vocabulary.

evidence_ref.description: Optional reference to claim disclosure, presentation response, or invite proof that triggered this consent (audit trail).

consent_revoke_payload.description: Revoke a previously granted consent. Wire-equivalent to a Control Move whose effect is remove(tag) on the consent cell ak:cell:ak.component.consent.grant.v1:<consent_id> (the same cell written by ak.consent.grant). Payload observed_dots MUST match the Control Move effect's observed_dots so schema validation and audit can see exactly what was removed.

consent_id.description: MUST equal the consent_id of the ak.consent.grant being revoked.

observed_dots.description: Exact add dots being removed. A full revoke, including consent_scope=any cascade, MUST enumerate every active dot that becomes inactive; implicit cascade without dot enumeration is invalid.

contact_accepted_payload.description: Holder-signed normal Contact acceptance fact. This is version 1 of the issuer-local directional lineage. It grants only the explicit Contact scopes and neither reads nor writes Consent.

previous_terminal_contact_round_id.description: Required by semantic admission when the accepted request is a recontact. It MUST equal the same field in the referenced request fact and its source-signed acceptance receipt. It is absent for a root Contact round.

contact_rejected_payload.description: Holder-signed terminal rejection of one exact accepted request. It establishes no Contact round and carries no Consent or Contact round evidence fields.

contact_requested_payload.description: Requester-signed directional Contact request fact. It is created before any acceptance receipt or basis exists, so neither may appear in this payload. It grants only the requester's explicit Contact scopes and neither reads nor writes Consent.

introduction_evidence_digest.description: Required digest of the exact private introduction_evidence carried by the request branch of ak.peer.contacts.command.submit. Raw evidence is not written into the contact fact log.

previous_terminal_contact_round_id.description: Requester-signed immediate predecessor link for recontact. It is required when this request follows a previously accepted terminal Contact round and forbidden for a root request. It is not the issuer-local request-slot predecessor.

contact_tombstoned_payload.description: Holder-signed terminal event for one issuer-local Contact lineage. The event kind itself supplies terminal semantics; the payload carries only the exact peer, basis and predecessor coordinates. It does not read, write or revoke Consent.

mentions.description: Structured direct mention AST nodes for this Content Block. This is the only carrier of a direct mention: authorization, notification routing and audit attribution read mention_node.subject_id exclusively (zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.1-§9.4.2).

audience_mentions.description: Structured broadcast mention AST nodes for this Content Block (zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.3).

attachments.description: Profile-defined attachment hints. At most 32; canonical durable attachment relations SHOULD use Relation attached_to.

not.$comment: Reject discriminator field name `type`, composite child array name `blocks`, and byte-count field `size`. The discriminator is `kind`, the composite child array is `parts`, and byte counts use `size_bytes` (see schemas/message.schema.json and forbidden-wire-fields.json `blocks/content_block_composite`).

body.description: Inline text body. Authoritative bound is 256 KiB UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound. Longer bodies MUST use ak.content.long_text (zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4).

content_block_long_text.description: ak.content.long_text: plain text whose full normalized UTF-8 body exceeds the 256 KiB inline boundary (or, by the narrow exception in zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4, whose Event would otherwise exceed the 1 MiB envelope limit). Exactly one of the plaintext branch (blob_ref + size_bytes + media_type) and the E2EE branch (attachment) applies. v1 core Content Block: no feature gate, no server-side opt-out.

format.description: Closed set for long text. prosemirror_json is forbidden here; structured rich text needs its own Content Block.

body.description: Inline fallback. Authoritative bound is 4096 UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound.

blob_ref.description: Hash-addressed Blob ref for the full normalized UTF-8 body. UUID blob refs are forbidden here because they carry no digest commitment.

size_bytes.description: Normalized full UTF-8 body bytes. The >256 KiB rule and the narrow Event-overflow exception are normative validator rules (zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4), not a schema minimum.

media_type.description: MUST match format. No parameters: charset is fixed to UTF-8 by this kind.

format.description: Closed set for long text. prosemirror_json is forbidden here; structured rich text needs its own Content Block.

body.description: Inline fallback. Authoritative bound is 4096 UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound.

attachment.description: Encrypted full-body Blob descriptor. MUST use scheme ak.blob.stream_aead.v1 with the matching _stream alg; whole-file AEAD is forbidden for long text.

blob_ref.description: Long text MUST use a hash-addressed Blob ref; the <suite>:<hex> part MUST equal attachment.ciphertext_digest and the Blob metadata content_digest.

size_bytes.description: Normalized full UTF-8 plaintext body bytes; encrypted_attachment.size_bytes is the plaintext count that segment_count = ceil(size_bytes / segment_bytes) is derived from (zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md section 3.1 / 3.3.1). The >256 KiB rule and the narrow Event-overflow exception are normative validator rules, not a schema minimum.

device_authorize_payload.description: Closed authorization record shared by registration genesis, PCR-policy recovery, and accepted-device pairing. registration_anchor and pcr_recovery use a candidate-device possession proof over the full authorization core; pcr_recovery is admitted only beside an accepted recovery session and monotonic PCR generation CAS. accepted_device uses the current accepted approving device. None of these branches derives human authority from current DID state.

hpke_key.description: Device HPKE public key used for secret/key envelope sealing. It is covered by the possession transcript and by the surrounding root anchor or accepted-device Event proof; services MUST NOT substitute it. For accepted_device pairing its authority is the target device_pairing_target_attestation, which the approving device reads only after that attestation verifies.

algorithms.description: Canonical sorted unique algorithm ids supported by this device. Enters device trust binding transcript together with device_public_key and hpke_key. For accepted_device pairing its authority is the target device_pairing_target_attestation, not any service-supplied or staged copy.

authorized_by.description: Under registration_anchor this is the principal whose durable registration control evidence was accepted. Under pcr_recovery it is the same principal selected by the recovery session and account-local lineage. Under accepted_device it is the approving device id at the accepted generation.

authorization_binding_kind.description: registration_anchor is valid only in accepted PCR genesis; pcr_recovery only in a recovery unit authorized by the accepted PCR recovery policy; accepted_device requires an active approving device. No branch permits a same-core foreign PCR lineage.

device_signature.description: Required Ed25519 possession proof. registration_anchor uses ak.device-authorize-possession-proof-v1, pcr_recovery uses ak.device-authorize-recovery-possession-proof-v1, and accepted_device uses ak.device-authorize-accepted-device-possession-proof-v1. All transcripts bind authorization_binding_kind and cannot be substituted across branches.

recovery_session_id.description: Required by the pcr_recovery branch and omitted for registration_anchor and ordinary accepted_device pairing.

device_reanchor_payload.description: Closed account-local PCR recovery payload. The account authority is selected by principal_id plus principal_server_id and one monotonic local device-generation CAS. PCR realm/frontier identifiers remain local recovery state and are not an external principal identity selector.

new_device_generation.description: Must be the immediate monotonic successor of previous_device_generation.

did_root_evidence_digest.description: Required only when recovery_authority_kind=did_root; proves the optional factor enabled by the frozen PCR policy.

replacement_authorize_payload_digest.description: canonical_digest of the replacement ak.device.authorize payload object, using the Realm live digest suite.

device_revoke_payload.description: Payload for ak.device.revoke. The revocation's control-plane authorization basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis (covered by the canonical event bytes and proofs); its permanent cutoff is the accepted Seal covering this Move. First durable canonical acceptance atomically creates ak.schema.device_revocation_state.v1 revocation_pending for the exact reducer-derived current device authorization and generation. The payload carries no frontier or generation field, and producers cannot self-report derived pending selectors.

direct_conversation_authorization_basis.description: Canonical authorization basis for creating a Direct Conversation. accepted_contact carries exactly the accepted contact request/accept refs. managed_agent_controller carries exactly two unique accepted Event refs: the controller-authored ak.agent.provision Event, whose payload already binds the Agent, controller, delegation, accountability and selector facts, and the current active ak.agent.key.authorize Event. The retired accountability-grant plus selector-claim provisioning pair is invalid here.

direct_conversation_bound_payload.description: Participant endorsement of the settled Direct Conversation coordinates and of the first exact-pair MLS generation. It does not enforce uniqueness: at most one Realm can exist per pair because only the founder derived from the pair's root Contact round may author the founding unit. Written once and never retired, so it carries no binding_state, no supersedes ref and no permanent mls_group_id; participant authority always reads the current active MLS generation. binding_digest is a receiver-derived off-wire semantic digest over the closed normalized binding object defined by contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 8.3 and MUST NOT be added to this payload.

pair_key.description: Canonical unordered pair key: SHA-256(UTF8(ak.direct-conversation.pair-key.v1 followed by LF) || JCS({participants:[p0,p1],trust_domain_id})) where p0/p1 are canonical stable subject DIDs sorted by unsigned UTF-8 byte order. Receivers MUST recompute it exactly as contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 5.1 defines; handles and unresolved pairwise DIDs are forbidden inputs.

founding_unit_digest.description: Digest of the accepted four Event atomic founding unit this binding endorses.

initial_exact_pair_generation_ref.description: The generation 1 ak.direct_conversation.mls_generation.activate Event: the first exact-pair active MLS generation. Audit only; evaluators read the current active value.

direct_conversation_mls_generation_activ.description: Selects which already-established MLS group currently holds send authority in a Direct Conversation Realm. It never creates a group. Generation 0 is the founder's sender-only provisional exporter group. Generation 1 MUST be authored by the joiner: no portable proof exists that the peer Principal Server durably accepted the Welcome, so only the joiner can truthfully assert it, mirroring the rule that consume is never proxied. Generation 2 and above are post-binding repair and require generation = current + 1 with predecessor_active_value_digest matching the current value.

pair_key.description: Canonical unordered pair key: SHA-256(UTF8(ak.direct-conversation.pair-key.v1 followed by LF) || JCS({participants:[p0,p1],trust_domain_id})) where p0/p1 are canonical stable subject DIDs sorted by unsigned UTF-8 byte order. Receivers MUST recompute it exactly as contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 5.1 defines; handles and unresolved pairwise DIDs are forbidden inputs.

predecessor_active_value_digest.description: Absent for generation 0; otherwise MUST equal the current active value digest.

default_key_share.description: Baseline key-share rule before restricted_rules are evaluated. event_time_visibility still requires T0 history visibility, current safety policy, and receiver device checks.

allowed_receiver_states.description: Closed baseline key-share receiver-state allow-list. This is intentionally narrower than restricted_rules[].receiver_classes: preview_token_holder is a read/preview class, not a key-share state, and MUST never be inferred here or receive history key material solely from a preview token.

receiver_classes.description: Read-eligibility classes for this restricted rule. This axis intentionally includes preview_token_holder, unlike value.allowed_receiver_states. A preview token may authorize a bounded stub/projection but never satisfies the independent key-share receiver-state gate.

restricted_policy_digest.description: Required when value=restricted. Digest of the effective ak.realm.history_sharing_policy value that defines restricted history visibility.

identity_disclosure_policy_state_payload.description: Identity disclosure-policy state payload. policy_id is the stable policy cell subject.

identity_disclosure_receipt_state_payloa.description: Identity disclosure-receipt log payload. holder_principal_id is the stable log subject.

identity_presentation_request_state_payl.description: Identity presentation-request log payload. request_id is the stable presentation correlation subject.

invitee.description: Directed invite subject DID. The Invite id is derived from this Event's event_id and MUST NOT be carried in the genesis payload.

invite_delivery_target.description: Public durable target for private invite delivery. payload.invitee is the subject; this object carries only the recipient Principal Server service DID.

introduction_evidence_digest.description: Digest of private invite delivery introduction_evidence. Raw locator tokens and receive-policy state MUST NOT appear in durable Realm events.

expires_at.description: Invite expiry timestamp. Directed v1 invite creates MUST carry it; reducers MUST NOT infer indefinite validity.

third_party_id.description: Third-party invite genesis material. The Invite id is derived from this Event's event_id and MUST NOT be carried in the payload.

delivery_status.description: Initial effective member delivery status; subject is the accepting Event actor.

invitee.description: MUST equal the directed invite's stored invitee so invite.lifecycle and member.state move atomically.
Required for a directed invite and forbidden by semantic admission for a 3PID placeholder.

target_state.description: Terminal invalidation of a pending invite, carried by an authorized writer's signed Control Move. send_failed and expired are observations the writer commits explicitly (third-party-invites.md 6.1); neither may be written by a local timer or delivery retry loop.

subject_id.description: Subject DID being bound by a ak.invite.claim payload. For claim payloads this MUST match binding_proof.subject_id and the DID verification method used by subject_proof.

token_commitment.description: Reducer-matched salted commitment for the pending ak.invite.third_party record. Raw invite tokens, URL fragments, SMS codes, or plaintext 3PID values MUST NOT appear on wire.

claim_nonce.description: One-time nonce scoped to (invite_id, token_commitment). Reducers MUST reject nonce replay while preserving non-enumerable external responses.

binding_proof.description: Verification-service proof for ak.invite.claim. Reducers verify signature over the ak.invite.claim.binding_proof.v1 transcript against the invite's verification_public_key and current Realm verification_service_id allowlist before accepting a claimed transition.

verification_service_id.description: Verification service DID. Realm reducers MUST re-check this DID against the current effective Realm allowlist and any service DID pinned by the original invite.

verification_method.description: DID URL with required key fragment. Method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0; matches the strict form used by $defs/verification_method elsewhere in this schema.

subject_id.description: DID being bound by the verification service. MUST equal the payload top-level subject_id.

realm_id.description: Realm bound into the verification-service proof. MUST equal the Event envelope realm_id.

claim_nonce.description: Nonce bound into the verification-service proof. MUST equal the payload top-level claim_nonce.

expires_at.description: Proof expiration. Reducers MUST reject expired proofs and MUST also enforce the invite cell expires_at.

signature.description: Signature over utf8("ak.invite.claim.binding_proof.v1\n") || canonical_json({audience, binding_proof: unsigned_binding_proof, claim_nonce, invite_digest, invite_id, realm_id, subject_id, token_commitment, verification_service_id}); unsigned_binding_proof is this object without signature.

subject_proof.description: Subject DID proof over ak.invite.claim.subject_proof.v1 transcript. The transcript digest binds subject_id, invite_id, realm_id, token_commitment, claim_nonce, audience, verification_service_id, and binding_proof_digest of the complete signed binding_proof object.

transcript_digest.description: Digest of the canonical ak.invite.claim.subject_proof.v1 transcript.

join_policy_component.$comment: Value shape of the join_policy component of realm_policy_bundle_payload; it has no separate Event kind and no separate cell family, and rides inside the ak.component.realm.policy_bundle.v1 cas_register value. Structural validation is JSON Schema; property-level gate_id uniqueness within gates[] cannot be expressed in pure JSON Schema 2020-12, so it is enforced by (a) reducer rejection with reason_code=join_policy_duplicate_gate_id and (b) tools/lint_artifacts.py check_join_policy_gate_id_uniqueness over fixtures and Markdown examples. uniqueItems below catches whole-object duplicates as a baseline. See zh/governance/join-policy.md §3 / §3.1.

application_ttl.description: Join application pending lifetime as an ISO 8601 duration, e.g. PT168H.

cooldown_after_reject.description: Minimum interval before the same actor may reapply after rejection, as an ISO 8601 duration, e.g. PT72H.

key_backup_active_series_payload.description: Payload for ak.key_backup.active_series. The standalone ak.schema.key_backup_active_series.v1 schema carries the authoritative signed active-series record shape.

keypackage_ref.description: Opaque content-addressed or service-scoped MLS KeyPackage reference. Hash-shaped refs MUST use keypackage_digest for digest bytes.

member_delivery_binding.description: Per-Realm binding of a member to a concrete delivery target service. Authoritative source for Realm-scoped event / sync / to-device / push / key-package delivery; sender MUST NOT consult the actor's DID Document service entry as an alternative resolution path when this binding is present. Pairwise / unlinkability use-cases are orthogonal — see identity-did.md and pairwise DID guidance.

recipient_service_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the recipient Principal Server for this member in this Realm.

recipient_service_kind.description: v1 only allows principal_server. Realm Event fanout is derived solely from effective joined-member delivery bindings and deduplicated by recipient_service_id.

binding_scope.description: v1 only allows realm-scoped bindings. Organization-wide or DID-global bindings are out of v1 scope; they would be expressed by Realm policy + organization registry instead.

binding_source.description: How the binding was determined at join time. 'explicit' = user / admin chose; 'did_document_default' = resolved from invitee DID Document (only allowed when Realm policy enables fallback); other values are policy-driven.

delivery_modes.description: Explicit allow-list of delivery modes for this binding. Empty / absent is NOT permitted; implementations declaring a 'full' member SHOULD list all five values.

service_resolution.description: Signed first-hop ServiceResolutionRecord inline or by digest-bound reference. Senders validate it and MAY maintain an implementation-local TTL route cache; the cache is not protocol authority.

did_document_digest.description: Canonical hash of invitee's DID Document at resolved_at. Required when binding_source = did_document_default.

resolved_at.description: Wall-clock time at which the binding was resolved. Always required so that downstream verifiers can decide whether the resolved state is still acceptable under their freshness policy.

service_acceptance_ref.description: Reference to the recipient service's prior service_acceptance / endorsement Event. Required when binding_source = explicit, invite, or organization_policy; reducer MUST verify the referenced Event is signed by recipient_service_id and its scope covers this Realm. Producers MUST NOT fabricate this ref for realm bootstrap; bootstrap without real service evidence must use another binding_source with its own evidence or remain unroutable.

holder_proof_ref.description: Reference to the member's DID proof (challenge-response) that bound the DID to recipient_service_id at the auth/account layer. Required when the member did not submit the join Control Move directly from a session at recipient_service_id.

policy_event_ref.description: Reference to the Realm / Join / Organization policy revision that authorised this binding. Required when binding_source ∈ {join_policy, organization_policy, realm_policy}.

expires_at.description: Optional expiry. After this timestamp the binding is no longer usable for delivery; senders MUST quarantine pending events and the member MUST submit a rebind Move (same-state join self-transition) carrying a fresh binding. Sender behaviour is fail-closed: MUST NOT fall through to DID Document on expiry.

member_identity_update_payload.description: Payload for ak.member.identity.update. Append-only replacement event for one Realm-scoped member display/subject projection segment. Service-visible metadata names the segment and the prior events it replaces; the segment body is plaintext or the original encrypted envelope and MUST contain the complete data for that segment. Handle lifecycle is excluded from this event and is governed by ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 issuer claims.

segment.description: v1 core defines a single full MemberIdentity segment. Narrower segments require a future schema/profile revision that extends this enum or defines a new payload schema; v1 receivers MUST reject unknown segment values.

replaces.description: Prior ak.member.identity.update events in the same (realm_id, actor_id, segment) that this event supersedes for current profile projection. Referenced events remain immutable history.

payload_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of the replaced event's full payload.identity_payload carrier wrapper ({member_identity: ...} or {encrypted_payload: ...}). Prevents replacing a different payload under a reused or confused event id.

identity_payload_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of the exact identity_payload carrier object. It is a cache invalidation key, not a substitute for signature or MLS verification.

expected_state_digest.description: Optional optimistic concurrency guard for the current effective set of this (realm_id, actor_id, segment). When present, it MUST equal the writer-observed effective-set digest before applying this event: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON {realm_id, actor_id, segment, effective_events:[{event_id, segment, payload_digest}]}, with effective_events sorted by (segment,event_id). It is not the identity_payload_digest and not a roster member_display_state_digest.

gate_proofs.description: Join-policy gate proofs evaluated by governance/join-policy.md before accepting membership=join. maxItems aligns with the gates 1..16 bound in join_policy_component; see zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md.

reason.description: Bounded human-readable audit note. It never supplies membership authority or proves cascade provenance.

agent_controller_binding.description: Required by semantic admission for every Native Personal Agent join and every controller-membership-ended cleanup. Non-Agent membership MUST reject it.

membership_state.description: Canonical membership state enum shared by ak.member.state (Realm) and ak.circle.member.state (Circle). Single source of truth: Realm and Circle membership use the identical value set; they MUST NOT diverge. `knock` denotes a pending join request (Realm Join Policy / Circle join_rule=knock); see governance/join-policy.md §9 and models/circle.md §9.1.

subject_id.description: Authoritative mention target principal DID. For native personal agent selectors this is the agent principal DID, not the controller DID.

handle_at_time.description: Canonical handle snapshot at compose time. Audit / debug / search metadata only; renderers MUST resolve the current primary handle from subject_id instead (zh/identity/identity-handles.md §3.8.1-§3.8.2).

controller_subject_id.description: Audit metadata for @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> inputs. MUST NOT replace subject_id for routing, authorization, or attribution.

controller_handle_at_time.description: Canonical controller handle snapshot from an agent selector input. Audit / debug / search metadata only.

message_create_payload.description: Payload for ak.message.create. If content/encrypted_content contains an audience_mention AST node (for example @all or @here), reducer admission and notification dispatch MUST additionally enforce ak.message.mention.broadcast plus the audience policy / max_recipient / rate-limit rules in zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.3. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered.

allOf.$comment: ak.message.create payload MUST NOT carry revision_root. Reducer initializes revision_root := id on create; only ak.message.revise events may set it. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9 and forbidden-wire-fields.json `revision_root/message_create_payload`.

ak.message.create payload MUST NOT carry message_id. The materialized Message.id is obtained by retyping the creating Event.event_id's full 33-byte / 44-character token; a second identity would create a conflicting truth source. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9 and forbidden-wire-fields.json `message_id/message_create_payload`.

mention_sidecar_digest.description: Optional E2EE mention-routing sidecar tags for push-notification fallback. Tags are opaque keyed-HMAC routing tokens produced by the sender client only when Realm policy enables recipient_registered_token routing; services compare them to recipient-registered opaque tokens and MUST NOT derive MLS exporter secrets.

reply_to.description: Optional creation convenience: the message this one replies to. The reducer records it as the message's reply linkage (lifting it onto the message content) and surfaces it as a replies_to relation in the message projection; it does not require a separate canonical ak.relation event. The materialized Message object itself carries no reply_to scalar. See strand-and-message.md §9.1.

agent_context.description: Auditable authorization context required when a native Agent authors the message.

message_encrypted_content.description: MLS-protected Message ContentBlock bound to its one canonical decrypted schema.

message_encrypted_metadata.description: MLS-protected Message metadata bound to its one canonical decrypted schema.

message_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Message metadata. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

track_name.description: Active track_name of the redacted message's parent Strand. Optional: when omitted, reducers MUST resolve from the existing message. When present, MUST equal that resolved track_name.

message_revise_payload.description: Payload for ak.message.revise. Revisions that introduce new direct mentions MAY generate mention notifications only when the implementation can compare against the previous accepted visible revision. Revisions that introduce an audience_mention AST node (including @all / @here mappings) MUST satisfy the same ak.message.mention.broadcast and policy gates as create.

track_name.description: Active track_name of the target Strand. Optional on revise/redact: when omitted, reducers MUST resolve from the existing message identified by message_id / target_ref / revision_of. When present, MUST equal that resolved track_name.

mimi_room_binding_payload.description: Payload for ak.mimi.room_binding. Writes the ak.component.mimi.room_binding.v1 cell whose subject is payload.mimi_room_uri (see event-kind-registry.json cell_subject). Authoritative field set: zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §3. The binding is a projection of an Arkret Realm/Strand discussion track into a MIMI room; it is not canonical truth. Creation / update / revocation MUST hold ak.policy.manage, ak.realm.admin, or an equivalent interop capability. E2EE MIMI rooms MUST bind mls_group_id and pass the active MLS security_frontier_digest gate.

mimi_room_uri.description: Canonical MIMI room URI and the cell subject source for ak.component.mimi.room_binding.v1 (registry cell_subject.kind = uri). The closed canonical form and the full percent-encoding that turns it into a CellRef subject are defined in zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md section 4 and zh/conformance/encoding.md section 4; a non-canonical spelling MUST be rejected with schema_violation rather than normalized.

binding_scope.description: Arkret Realm + Strand scope this MIMI room projects. strand_id MUST point at an accepted Strand with discussion track enabled inside realm_id; the MIMI room timeline only projects that Strand's discussion track.

hub_provider.description: Service DID explicitly delegated by Realm policy, Organization DID, or participant DID to host the hub role.

mls_group_id.description: MLS group id. MUST be present for E2EE MIMI rooms.

policy_root.description: Digest of the Arkret policy component projection bound to this MIMI room binding.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the binding. Initial status MUST be proposed or accepted; legal transitions are defined in zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2. accepted bindings authorize projection; revoked bindings stop new MIMI writes; migrating stops new writes until a verified migration proof returns the binding to accepted or revoked.

base_epoch.description: Expected previous MLS epoch. MUST equal governance_binding.previous_epoch.

next_epoch.description: Committed next MLS epoch. MUST equal governance_binding.next_epoch.

commit_bytes_b64.description: Unpadded base64url RFC 9420 MLS Commit message. Receivers verify commit_digest before applying it.

mls_genesis_payload.$comment: Schema requires both effective_scope and governance_binding. Reducers/verifiers must additionally compare effective_scope with governance_binding.effective_scope; JSON Schema cannot express deep cross-field equality.

effective_scope.description: Tagged scope of the MLS group created at epoch 0. MUST match governance_binding.effective_scope.

group_info_ref.description: Content-addressed reference to the exact RFC 9420 GroupInfo bytes. The embedded sha256 value MUST equal group_info_digest without the sha256: prefix.

group_info_digest.description: SHA-256 of the raw bytes obtained by base64url-decoding group_info_bytes_b64 from the standard group-state-material operation.

ratchet_tree_ref.description: Content-addressed reference to the exact RFC 9420 ratchet_tree extension bytes for epoch 0. The embedded sha256 value MUST equal ratchet_tree_digest without the sha256: prefix.

ratchet_tree_digest.description: SHA-256 of the raw bytes obtained by base64url-decoding ratchet_tree_bytes_b64 from the standard group-state-material operation.

realm_id.description: Parent Realm identifier. MUST equal effective_scope.realm_id.

circle_id.description: Present only when effective_scope.kind='circle'. MUST equal effective_scope.circle_id.

sidecar_id.description: Present only when effective_scope.kind='sidecar'. MUST equal effective_scope.sidecar_id.

effective_scope.description: Tagged MLS governance scope. Realm-default groups use {kind:'realm', realm_id}; Circle groups use {kind:'circle', realm_id, circle_id}; Sidecar groups use {kind:'sidecar', realm_id, sidecar_id}. This field, not Strand id or track, determines key and participant scope.

security_frontier_digest.description: Canonical digest of the closed key-access frontier for this MLS scope: effective membership; only participant device/Agent keys referenced by current or pending MLS leaves; MLS group membership; and encryption/history policy that changes current or historical key access. Capability, ordinary metadata, moderation, routing, contact and consent-only facts are excluded unless their accepted effect actually removes an MLS leaf. Producers do not supply an arbitrary event list; every verifier rederives the digest from accepted Seal state.

sidecar_binding.description: Required exactly for effective_scope.kind='sidecar'; forbidden for Realm and Circle MLS scopes.

binding_profile.description: Explicit profile that defines how this governance binding is interpreted. Full E2EE uses ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1; the only v1 downgrade profile is ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1. Receivers MUST fail closed when this field is missing, unsupported, inconsistent with the Realm profile declaration, or used to imply a downgrade without the matching policy/profile declaration.

reducer_profile.description: Reducer profile used to derive the closed security_frontier_digest projection. Receivers MUST fail closed when this field does not equal the Realm reducer-profile cell at the binding's authenticated frontier.

mls_governance_binding.$comment: Schema requires tagged scope ID presence rules. Reducers/verifiers additionally compare realm_id and the circle_id/sidecar_id value against effective_scope; JSON Schema cannot express those cross-field string equalities.

keypackage_digest.description: Canonical hash of the MLS KeyPackage bytes identified by keypackage_ref.
Canonical hash of the claimed MLS KeyPackage bytes. MUST equal the referenced ak.mls.keypackage.payload.keypackage_digest and claim_ref.keypackage_digest.

claim_ref.description: KeyPackage claim binding validated before Welcome decryption. Exactly one trust binding is present: device_authorize_event_id for a PCR-authorized device or agent_key_authorize_event_id for an independently authorized Native Agent runtime.

agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted active ak.agent.key.authorize Event for the claimed Native Agent runtime key.

claim_envelope.description: Closed requester device-or-Native-Agent signature binding the claimed KeyPackage to this Welcome, Realm, claim nonce and Welcome digest before decrypting the Welcome. Signer authority is established by the accepted authorization Events and their in-envelope Principal Server admission proofs; no signer-evidence sidecar is carried.

claim_receipt.description: Destination-signed receipt used for both same-service and remote claims. The receiving destination Principal Server validates it against its durable claim ledger before accepting the Welcome.

moderation_decision_lift_payload.description: Payload for ak.moderation.decision.lift. Writes an or_set remove effect on the same ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell, removing exactly the dots enumerated in observed_dots, which MUST belong to the decision identified by decision_ref. See zh/authz/policy-server.md §7.1 and zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.2 (appeal verdict=overturn MUST pair a lift whose target equals decision_ref in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction).

target_ref.description: The moderated target whose ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell the lift mutates. Same cell subject as the original ak.moderation.decision.

decision_ref.description: Reference to the prior ak.moderation.decision Event whose sealed tag is being removed.

observed_dots.description: Exact add dots being removed. Every dot's event_id segment MUST equal the complete EventId token of decision_ref, so a lift can only revoke the appealed decision; adds from other issuers stay active and keep folding by hard_deny > quarantine > require_review. A lift is a partial revocation, so or_set_remove_observed is forbidden here - it would remove every surviving add on the cell. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2 and zh/governance/content-moderation.md section 5.5.2.

moderation_decision_payload.description: Payload for ak.moderation.decision. A sealed moderation decision that writes an or_set add effect onto the ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell whose subject is target_ref. Multiple active adds fold by hard_deny > quarantine > require_review > none. dismiss is valid only when target_ref identifies the report Event being closed and contributes none to the content verdict fold. Runtime allow and soft_deny remain out-of-band outcomes. The actor MUST independently hold the registered ak.moderation.decision capability.

target_ref.description: The moderated target (event / object). Canonical string of this ref is the ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell subject.

decision.description: Sealed moderation-state decision verb. dismiss only resolves a report queue item and does not loosen the target content verdict. allow and soft_deny are out-of-band runtime outcomes.

issuer.description: Actor or service DID issuing the sealed moderation decision. Reducers use it as part of the or_set add tag and appeal separation-of-duties check.

request_canonical_digest.description: JCS SHA-256 digest of the moderated request or event preview bound to the Policy Server decision. Part of the moderation_state or_set add tag.

action.description: Optional finer-grained §5.3 moderation_policy action family entry that the decision verb maps to (content-moderation.md §8.1).

reason_code.description: Machine-readable diagnostic. Values that cross service or federation boundaries MUST be registered in error-code-registry.json reason_codes.

policy_decision_ref.description: Reference to the Policy Server signed decision used as risk evidence. Audit / replay only; not a capability source.

modify_decision_ref.description: Set when this decision is the new decision emitted atomically by an appeal verdict=modify (content-moderation.md §5.5.2); reducer verifies it matches the same-batch appeal event id.

effective_scope.description: Governance boundary for the report. Defaults to the Realm scope when absent; Circle-scoped targets MUST resolve to the target Circle and route only to scoped moderators/admins.

provenance.description: Admission discriminator (contract-registry admission_variants). Absent or "self": the reporter's own device authored the Event (self_authored_proof, actor == reporter). "mimi_facade": the Event is service-authored by the MIMI provider facade (service_attested); reporter carries the Arkret principal resolved under extensions/mimi-interop.md section 10/11, and source_provider is required.

source_provider.description: Origin MIMI provider's service DID for a facade-mapped report. Required exactly when provenance is "mimi_facade"; forbidden otherwise.

morph_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Morph object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

not.$comment: zh/models/common-fields.md: the object id is derived from this create Event's own event_id; carrying it in the payload is schema_violation reason object_id_not_event_derived.

morph_schema_migrate_payload.description: Migration of a Morph's schema_refs[] under the schema-evolution policy (zh/models/morph.md §4.1 S3). Distinct from ak.morph.update — schema_refs[] changes MUST go through this event so the migration is auditable, capability-gated, and carries an explicit compatibility class. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds the ak.morph.schema_migrate capability (or the Realm-declared equivalent) at the event's frontier; missing capability yields capability_denied. Reducer MUST reject compatibility_class ∈ {breaking, transformation} unless the Realm declares ak.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1 (yielding morph_schema_refs_transformation_unsupported otherwise). Reducer MUST verify from_schema_refs[] matches the Morph's current schema_refs[] at apply time (yielding failed_precondition otherwise). The event's own requirements.schema[] MUST include the union of from_schema_refs[] and to_schema_refs[] so readers can resolve both versions during overlap. Each transformation_rules[] entry SHOULD describe a deterministic, replay-safe per-field mapping (rename, type widening, default backfill, etc.); the rule object shape is governed by the Realm-declared ak.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1 profile.

from_schema_refs.description: Expected current schema_refs[] of the Morph at apply time. Reducer MUST set-equal-compare against the Morph's state and reject mismatches as failed_precondition (semantic: optimistic concurrency on schema_refs).

to_schema_refs.description: Desired schema_refs[] after migration. MUST be a registered set of schema profile ids resolvable at apply time.

compatibility_class.description: additive: to_schema_refs[] only adds optional fields / lookup-compatible profile refs; no historical event needs reinterpretation. breaking: to_schema_refs[] removes or tightens fields; future events follow new schema but historical events keep validating under from_schema_refs[]. transformation: a per-event data transform is needed to map old payload shape to new (requires explicit transformation rules). Core reducers MUST accept additive only; breaking and transformation require the ak.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1 opt-in Realm profile.

transformation_rules.description: Required when compatibility_class='transformation'. Each entry MUST describe a deterministic, replay-safe per-field mapping (rename, type widening, default backfill, etc.). The rule object shape is governed by ak.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1 (see profile description in conformance-profiles.json).

migration_evidence.description: Optional seal / witness evidence justifying the migration (e.g., governance proposal id, audit trail seal). The event's authorization_ref carries the formal capability gate; migration_evidence is for human reviewers.

morph_stage_set_payload.description: Payload class for ak.morph.stage.set. Mutates Morph.stage / Morph.stage_changed_at. Intentionally carries no reason field — see the shared stage-set contract in zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3 and zh/models/morph.md §2.

not.$comment: Stage-set guard shared by the concrete Strand and Morph payload classes.

morph_update_payload.description: Payload class for ak.morph.update. Patches ordinary Morph fields on the Morph identified by target_ref. morph_kind is create-locked by ak.morph.create and MUST NOT appear in patch; stage and stage_changed_at are single-sourced by ak.morph.stage.set.

notary_fault_censorship_payload.description: Notary censorship evidence: a signed control-plane receipt whose event digest is provably absent from the obliged Seal's control_event_set_root and that received neither signed-reject nor defer. Does NOT automatically disqualify the notary; adds an audit fault record. See authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2.

receipt.description: The signed control-plane receipt issued under proposal_intake_sla_ms (event_digest, received_at, receipt_seq, issuer, signature).

seal_ref.description: The Seal that was obliged to include / signed-reject / defer the receipted Control Move.

non_membership_proof.description: Sorted-neighbor non-membership proof for the receipted event digest against seal_ref's control_event_set_root.

missing_rejection_or_defer_proof.description: Optional structured evidence that no signed-reject / defer covering the receipt exists in the obliged window.

notary_fault_equivocation_payload.description: Notary equivocation evidence: two Seals signed by signer_id that violate the slot rule (same (realm_id, notary_seq) with different canonical bytes, or notary_seq=k+1 not descending from the same signer's notary_seq=k). Admission is verification-only: the two conflicting notary signatures are the complete authorization; no capability grant is consulted. See authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1.

object_lifecycle_payload.description: Generic lifecycle payload for Strand / Circle / Morph archive-restore-tombstone style events. The target object is single-sourced by target_ref; target_state may describe the intended lifecycle result but cannot replace the target object reference.

not.$comment: Object kind is derived from the typed-id prefix on `id`; `type` is a banned field name.

object_snapshot.description: Embedded object snapshot inside an Event payload. Object kind is derived from the typed-id prefix on `id`; there is no separate `type` field.

or_set_dot.description: Canonical OR-Set dot: "ak:event:" + event_id + ":" + write_index, where write_index is the 0-based index of the write in the event kind's registry cell_writes[]. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2.

organization_discovery_state_payload.description: State payload for an Organization discovery declaration. organization_principal_id is the stable cell subject.

organization_moderation_policy_state_pay.description: Organization moderation-policy state. A producer identifies the Organization by exactly one canonical DID or typed Organization id; the first present identifier is the registered coalesce subject.

participant_binding.description: Token issuer's signed commitment over (realm_id, call_id, focus_id, actor_id, device_id, participant_identity, expires_at) for a media participant. See crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3 and crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1. v1 uses the single scheme ak.media.participant_binding.v1.

issuer_kid.description: DID URL (with fragment) of the token issuer service signing key. MUST resolve to a service DID present in the current-epoch ak.realm.media_service.service_id.

data_classes.description: Closed machine-checkable classes of plaintext or reversible derived content this service may receive. Human-readable purposes do not replace this field.

policy_action_state_payload.description: Policy action-log payload. Exactly one policy_id or action_id is present and becomes the registered coalesce subject.

policy_rule_state_payload.description: Policy rule state payload. rule_id is the stable ak.component.policy.rule.v1 cell subject and MUST equal the rule_id of the PolicyRule this event asserts, whose closed shape is defined by policy.schema.json #/$defs/policy_rule (zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5). The cell is an ordered_log, so each accepted event appends one revision rather than replacing the previous one.

rule_id.description: Rule identifier, same lexical form as policy.schema.json #/$defs/policy_rule rule_id.

policy_set_state_payload.description: Policy definition state payload. policy_id is the stable policy cell subject.

profile_realm_override_payload.description: Realm-scoped actor profile override payload for ak.profile.realm_override. target_ref is the Actor Profile being overridden; target_realm_id is the Realm where the override applies.

reaction_encrypted_payload_plaintext.description: Plaintext JSON encrypted into reaction_payload.encrypted_payload.ciphertext for ak.reaction.add / ak.reaction.remove in E2EE realms. The outer reaction_payload.key remains required and carries the service-visible routing tag; this plaintext carries the real reaction key and optional user content.

key.description: Canonical reaction key after client-side normalization: a single NFC Unicode emoji cluster or profile-registered short tag. This is the real reaction key, not the outer HMAC routing tag.

annotation.description: Optional user-visible annotation associated with the reaction.

remove_add_event_ids.description: Optional client-side convergence accelerator for ak.reaction.remove: add event ids that this remove intends to tombstone. MUST be omitted on ak.reaction.add. Service-side reducers still rely on the outer event actor_id, target_ref, key, and causal frontier.

reaction_payload.description: Reducer input for ak.reaction.add and ak.reaction.remove. The cell is a core OR-Set of reaction assertions and both kinds project one or_set_add; default-view membership is keyed on (actor_id, target_ref, key), and a remove tombstones every add from the same actor with the same key that is not strictly causally later than it, which includes the adds concurrent with it. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.8 for the authoritative Reaction model (target scope, OR-Set, authz, anti-abuse) and zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.9 for the plaintext-vs-encrypted policy.

key.description: Reaction key. Plaintext realms SHOULD use a single Unicode emoji cluster or registered short tag.
